recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

recR9a4OItodWBnvP.Bio: Emily Ridout is a folklorist and AstroYoga specialist who blends astrology, yoga, and tarot; she appeared on InnerVerse (multiple times) to discuss her book AstroYoga for an Aquarian Age.
recR9a4OItodWBnvP.Name: Emily Ridout

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Astrology as a Map for Change", "body": "Emily Ridout described her six week Astrology Academy, which she said was built to take students from beginners to readers of their own charts. She argued that horoscopes were less useful than learning the symbolism, because a chart works like a map for goals such as money, relationships and spiritual growth. She said she taught every yoga class with the current transits in mind and that a flow could shift brain and body chemistry toward a chosen change. Chance asked how far free will shapes reality and said looking at life as options was more interesting than fatalism."}, {"title": "Eclipse Season and the Unseen Venus", "body": "Emily explained that eclipse season begins when the sun sits within eighteen degrees of the lunar nodes, and she placed its start on October 19 with a partial eclipse near an invisible Venus. She argued that eclipses redirect people quickly, pushing them back on track in ways that feel either frustrating or freeing, and she advised against rash life decisions while Venus was out of sight. She described the November 8 lunar eclipse as transformation in the form of water and urged listeners to guard their minds and imagine a better world rather than buy into collective dreams of disaster."}, {"title": "Symbols, Letters, and Royal Ciphers", "body": "One speaker linked the Hanged Man's toes to the Tau, the cross and the letter T, arguing that these shapes carried solar and creative meaning across several traditions. Emily added that the circle, the cross and the crescent made up every planetary glyph. Later a speaker argued that King Charles's cipher carried the number 93, tied it to Neptunium and an eclipse code, and traced the word cipher to the Hebrew root behind the Sephiroth. Another voice wondered about the Rosy Cross, and a speaker speculated that calling a monogram a cipher hinted at playing a character."}, {"title": "Libra, Karma, and Seeing Clearly", "body": "Emily argued that Libra's scales, an inanimate object that still moves and can be manipulated, stood for the mechanical law of karma, meaning the predictable reaction to any action. She said Libra season offered a chance to see the actions at play and alter one's own karma, and she used cooking a pot of soup as her example. One speaker described karma and sin as natural consequence rather than cosmic score keeping, quoting comedian Owen Benjamin that sin makes you weaker. Another speaker wondered whether the earth itself worked as a living Akashic record, and a reply tied the Torah, Saturn and right measure to that idea."}, {"title": "Whether the Age of Aquarius Has Arrived", "body": "One speaker said they doubted the dawning of the Age of Aquarius, comparing the promise to utopian pitches from political movements and scientism, and claimed that calculations credited to Julius Caesar's astrologers put its start around 1746. Another speaker agreed that new age culture had rushed to paint the age in exciting terms, but argued that people alive today were dismantling an old system of control. Emily had earlier explained that the zodiac's slow drift against the stars changed what a chart meant. Later a speaker floated a sweater metaphor for the money system, and talk turned to a new zodiac."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Astro-Yoga Instructor Emily Ridout returns to Vibe Rant to talk esoteric astrology, eclipses, and taking advantage of obstacles to author our own world. Is the Age of Aquarius coming? Are we already in it? Or is the entire idea of the great cycles a fabricated construct? Astrology is pretty nuts.
